name: One-Time/Perpetual selling model PricingTermCount=1
what_it_tests: A perpetual/one-time line gets PricingTermCount stamped to the one-time constant so Subscription Pricing computes a single-term price; order creates Activated non-subscription Asset and recognizes full revenue
expected_behavior: PricingTermCount=1; ItemNetTotalPrice = NetUnitPrice * Qty * 1; Asset.IsSubscription=false, full revenue recognized
test_setup: Perpetual software (e.g. Cobalt Strike), One-Time/Perpetual, Qty=1-4, USD, Direct, no support

prior_run.actual: Fresh quote 00781543, Abstract OneTime Qty=2 list 2200. Force-reprice (CompletedWithPricing): NetUnitPrice=2200, NetTotalPrice=4400=2200*2, Subtotal=4400, Quote TotalPrice=4400, SellingModelType=OneTime. PricingTermCount=0 (not 1) - V21 OneTimePricingTermCountConstant=0 by design; price uses separate PricingTermCountValueOneConstant=1 so total NOT zeroed.
prior_run.evidence: https://fortra--uat.sandbox.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Quote/0Q0WC000003FcG90AK/view ; QLI 0QLWC000003kli94AA ; control quote 0Q0WC000003FN970AG OneTime lines also PTC=0 correct totals; ESD OneTimePricingTermCountConstant value=0
prior_run.notes: PricingTermCount field=0 deviates from catalog literal 'PricingTermCount=1' but is by-design: live V21 ESD declares OneTimePricingTermCountConstant=<value>0</value> (Assignment writer); a one-time charge has no recurring term. Price total correct because OneTime Subscription Pricing branch multiplies by separate PricingTermCountValueOneConstant=1. Reproduced on catalog control quote 0Q0WC000003FN970AG (both OneTime lines PTC=0, totals correct) - steady-state norm, not a regression.
